chunks: 4358 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Dawud al-Karkhi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: My wife has died, and she was compatible with me, and I have intended to marry. So he said:

Consider where you place yourself, and whom you make a شریک in your wealth, and to whom you disclose your religion, your secret, and your trust. If you must do so, then choose a virgin attributed to goodness and to good character,

Indeed, women have been created in different ways: among them is the gain and the burden, among them is the crescent when it appears to its possessor, and among them is darkness. So whoever attains the righteous among them will be fortunate, and whoever is defrauded has no revenge.

And they are three: a woman who is fertile and loving, who helps her husband through his time in his world and his hereafter, and does not assist time against him; a barren woman, neither possessing beauty nor character, and who does not help her husband in any good; and a loud, intrusive, fault-finding woman who deems much to be little and does not accept even a small amount.

key_terms.أَمَانَتِكَ: your trust and what is entrusted to your care
key_terms.بِكْرًا: a virgin, recommended here for marriage
key_terms.صَاحِبَتِي: my wife or female companion in marriage

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach about choosing a wife?
ai.summary: This hadith advises careful consideration in choosing a spouse, emphasizing trust, religion, character, and the deep personal partnership created by marriage. It describes differing dispositions among women and highlights the value of a righteous, supportive wife in one's worldly life and Hereafter.
